blocks.html: Zambia owes much of its reputation to its almost non-commercial safari industry. It has a very large number of family-run safaris and lodges – in fact, more than anywhere else in Africa.

blocks.orig: Their safari industry has developed over the years, which has led to an increase in the number of safari camps and an improvement in their quality as well. It is also the home of a new type of safari, the purest kind – night safari.
blocks.html: Over the years the safari industry here has grown, bringing more safari camps and better quality as well. Zambia is also where a new kind of safari comes from, the purest kind – the night safari.

blocks.orig: This night safari option is also the reason for Zambia having the most leopard sightings on the continent.
blocks.html: The option of night safaris is also why Zambia has the most leopard sightings on the continent.

blocks.orig: Zimbabwe is another beautiful country. May is one of the best times to go. It is the transitional month from wet to dry.
blocks.html: Zimbabwe is one more beautiful country. One of the best months to visit is May, when the wet season gives way to the dry.

blocks.orig: As the recent rainfall will keep the land looking green and succulent, the weather slowly becomes dry and temperatures drop at night.
blocks.html: The recent rain keeps the land green and lush, while the weather gradually turns dry and the nights get colder.

blocks.orig: In June the days will be warm but the nights cool. It is peak time for a safari and the drier weather will attract the animals to rivers and water holes, making animal spotting a lot easier.
blocks.html: June brings warm days and cool nights. It is peak safari time, and the drier weather draws the animals to rivers and waterholes, so spotting them becomes much easier.

blocks.orig: You will find elephants, leopards, zebras, lions, rhinos, and much more here. This country is also the home to Victoria Falls.
blocks.html: Elephants, leopards, zebras, lions, rhinos and much more live here, and the country is also home to Victoria Falls.

blocks.orig: There are many opportunities to view the wildlife in the vast desert country of Namibia. You may think it would be barren, but this would be wrong.
blocks.html: Namibia, a vast desert country, offers plenty of chances to watch wildlife. You might expect it to be barren, but you would be mistaken.

blocks.orig: There are many animals here who have learned to adapt to this harsh climate and limited environment.
blocks.html: Many animals here have learned to cope with the harsh climate and limited surroundings.

blocks.orig: The harsh but gorgeous Namib Desert is a coastal desert. Here you will find herds of elephants that traverse the desert, there will be different types of antelope, lions, and zebras.
blocks.html: The Namib Desert, harsh yet stunning, is a coastal desert. Herds of elephants cross it, and you will also find various kinds of antelope, as well as lions and zebras.

blocks.orig: Outside of this desert, the earlier month of March can be rainy and humid, however, April is usually drier. Rains will fall earlier on in the year and the country becomes more verdant around April.
blocks.html: Beyond the desert, March, earlier in the season, can be wet and humid, while April tends to be drier. The rains come earlier in the year, and by around April the country turns greener.

blocks.orig: Here are some tips to help you plan your first safari trip the right way!
blocks.html: These tips will help you plan your first safari trip the right way!

blocks.orig: Plan A Trip That Is Minimum of 8 Days In Tanzania
blocks.html: Plan a trip of at least 8 days in Tanzania

blocks.orig: Africa is very big, and each country inside this continent is just as big. A week’s holiday may seem ideal for some, but if you try to pack everything into just 7 days, including your flights you will be too rushed to enjoy it.
blocks.html: Africa is huge, and each of its countries is just as large. A week’s holiday may sound perfect to some, but if you squeeze everything into only 7 days, flights included, you will be in too much of a hurry to enjoy it.

blocks.orig: We recommend visiting for 8 days, plus your flight days as well. Doing it this way means you can enjoy everything the country offers and then have some time to relax as well.
blocks.html: Our advice is to stay for 8 days, plus the days you spend flying. That way you can enjoy all the country has to offer and still have time to relax.

blocks.orig: While normal safari trips are awesome, going to Tanzania for a long enough period of time can bring you other opportunities as well. Sure, go on the standard safari and experience everything up close and personal, but then do something else.
blocks.html: Regular safari trips are wonderful, but spending long enough in Tanzania opens up other possibilities too. By all means go on the standard safari and see everything up close, but then try something different.

blocks.orig: Take a hot air balloon safari as well. You now get to see everything from really far away as well. Take in the landscape in its full beauty from a bird’s eye view. If you can do both of these, you will have some sights you will never forget.
blocks.html: Add a hot air balloon safari, so that you see everything from high above as well. Enjoy the landscape in all its beauty from a bird’s eye view. Manage both and you will have sights you will never forget.

blocks.orig: Take the time to visit a Maasai village in Tanzania. Maasai present a very colorful sight in how their traditional dress stands out, with their rather ubiquitous spears in hand.
blocks.html: Make time for a visit to a Maasai village in Tanzania. The Maasai are a very colourful sight, their traditional dress standing out and their familiar spears in hand.

blocks.orig: The Maasai are nomadic sheep, cattle, and goat herders, and over time they have needed to adapt to modern ways. Most of whom have turned to agriculture, some even turned to live in cities.
blocks.html: Traditionally nomadic herders of sheep, cattle and goats, the Maasai have had to adapt to modern life over time. Most have taken up farming, and some have even moved to the cities.

blocks.orig: Some of the Maasai villages will be open for tourists to visit, they will entertain you with dances, including the infamous udumu.
blocks.html: A number of Maasai villages welcome tourists, and they will entertain you with dances, including the famous udumu.

blocks.orig: Relax On A Tropical Island After Your Safari
blocks.html: Unwind on a tropical island after your safari

blocks.orig: Once you are all done and dusted on your safari trip, why not take a chance to enjoy a different kind of nature?
blocks.html: When your safari trip is completely over and done with, why not take the opportunity to enjoy a different kind of nature?

blocks.orig: Tanzania has some of the most beautiful tropical beaches you will ever find in the world, and most of them are on the Tanzanian Islands.
blocks.html: Some of the most beautiful tropical beaches anywhere in the world are in Tanzania, and most of them lie on the Tanzanian Islands.

blocks.orig: Mafia, Zanzibar, and Pemba are all ideal pieces of heaven where you can unwind before or after your safari mainland venture.
blocks.html: Mafia, Zanzibar and Pemba are all perfect little pieces of heaven for relaxing before or after your safari on the mainland.

blocks.orig: On these islands, you can craft your itinerary to how you want it to be, including the island of your voice. Build your own trip, post safari, and relax by the ocean.
blocks.html: On these islands you can shape your itinerary exactly as you like, including the island of your choice. Put together your own post-safari trip and relax by the sea.

blocks.orig: Always keep an open mind when it comes to safaris, each trip will be unique and therefore, it is hard to predict anything. Do not stress over the things that you cannot control. You may not see a lot, or you might see everything.
blocks.html: Keep an open mind about safaris; every trip is different, so it is hard to predict anything. Don’t worry about what you cannot control. You might not see much, or you might see it all.

blocks.orig: The journey could be excessively long, or maybe it is a bit too tough. Setting expectations is never a good idea when faced with mother nature.
blocks.html: The journey may be very long, or perhaps a little too tough. With mother nature, having fixed expectations is never wise.

blocks.orig: You should also be flexible when it comes to safaris, and be prepared for warm or cold weather, blazing sun, or cool winds. Prepare for mosquitos and flies, for a rough ride, and more.
blocks.html: Be flexible on safari too, and ready for warm or cold weather, scorching sun or cool winds. Be prepared for mosquitos and flies, a bumpy ride and more.

blocks.orig: You will often be driving over sand and gravel, but the driver may cross a river, a field of stones, or just drive into the brush. You never know, be ready for anything that may come your way.
blocks.html: Much of the driving will be over sand and gravel, but your driver might also cross a river or a field of stones, or simply head into the bush. You never know, so be ready for whatever comes your way.

blocks.orig: Always follow the rules on a safari, rules are there for a reason, it is not a playground, and it can be very dangerous.
blocks.html: Always stick to the rules on safari. They exist for a reason: this is no playground, and it can be extremely dangerous.

blocks.orig: Do not approach elephants too closely, do not make a noise, keep hands and cameras inside the vehicles when near big cats and never stand between the water and a hippo.
blocks.html: Don’t get too close to elephants, keep quiet, keep your hands and cameras inside the vehicle near big cats, and never stand between a hippo and the water.

blocks.orig: We all know these rules. They are there for a reason, ensure that these rules are followed, and they are there for your safety after all.
blocks.html: We all know these rules, and they exist for a reason. Make sure they are followed – they are there to keep you safe, after all.

blocks.orig: Do not be embarrassed to ask as many questions as possible during a safari, the guides will be very wise and knowledgeable, and you will be able to learn a great deal about the animals and their behavior.
blocks.html: Don’t feel embarrassed about asking lots of questions on safari. The guides are very wise and well informed, and you can learn a lot about the animals and how they behave.

blocks.orig: Make use of the information stored away inside your tour guide’s brain, and ask away, even if you think it is a silly question, it is not.
blocks.html: Draw on everything your tour guide’s brain has stored and keep asking, even if a question seems silly to you – it isn’t.

blocks.orig: You may not want to make requests, maybe you are shy or anxious. Well, we are telling you to ask those things. See something in the distance and want to get your binoculars out for a better look, ask to stop.
blocks.html: Maybe you are shy or nervous and would rather not make requests. Well, we are telling you to ask anyway. If you spot something in the distance and want a better look through your binoculars, ask to stop.

blocks.orig: Want another picture of that hippo? Go for it. You are paying for the safari, and the guides are there to give you the best experience, if you want to stop, ask.
blocks.html: Fancy another photo of that hippo? Go ahead. You are paying for the safari, and the guides are there to give you the best experience, so if you would like to stop, just ask.

blocks.orig: You may think that you won’t want to keep the pictures because by the time you’ve seen 18 giraffes you won’t be taking that many anymore.
blocks.html: You might think you won’t want to keep all the photos, since after your 18th giraffe you won’t be taking as many.

blocks.orig: It is always good to take as many photos as you can, you never know when you may capture something you don’t want to forget!
blocks.html: Still, it is always worth taking as many photos as possible, as you never know when you might capture something you won’t want to forget!

blocks.orig: You never know if you will get a chance to get a picture that good again, so keep on going.
blocks.html: There is no telling whether you will ever get such a good shot again, so keep shooting.

blocks.orig: On your first trip you may see so much, so take as many pictures as you can, because the wildlife may be more sparse next time.
blocks.html: You may see a great deal on your first trip, so take as many photos as you can, as the wildlife could be harder to find next time.

blocks.orig: Safaris are one of the best and most exciting types of vacation, sure, they are also one of the most costly, but they take you into the heart of a place you will never forget, and may never go to again.
blocks.html: Safaris rank among the best and most exciting kinds of holiday. Yes, they are also among the most expensive, but they take you to the heart of a place you will never forget and may never visit again.

blocks.orig: These places are the heart and soul of the natural world, they are wonders that climate change could easily take away from us, so going out there and experiencing the beauty of what it is, is priceless.
blocks.html: These places are the heart and soul of the natural world, wonders that climate change could easily take from us, so going there and experiencing their beauty for yourself is priceless.

blocks.orig: Take the opportunity, and see these exotic wonderful animals in their true, natural homes by taking your first African safari!
blocks.html: Seize the chance to see these wonderful exotic animals in their true, natural homes on your first African safari!
